title: How to sum values between two dates
task: Total amounts that fall in a date range you specify — sales in a period, expenses between two dates.

excel.note: A = dates, B = amounts, D1/D2 = start/end dates in cells. Concatenate the operator with the date cell.

explanation: Two date conditions on the same column bracket the window: on-or-after the start AND on-or-before the end. In the verification the window is July 24-31, 2026, so the two rows in that range total 100+50 = 150 while the August-ish row (serial 46250) is excluded. Putting the start and end dates in cells (D1, D2) and concatenating them with & (">="&D1) makes the range adjustable without editing the formula — the basis of a date-filtered dashboard. The date column must hold real dates, not text. Use "<"&(D2+1) if D2 might carry a time component.
